CLINICAL HISTORY
Metastatic lung adenocarcinoma

TEST PERFORMED
Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) for ALK and ROS1 Gene Rearrangements

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue sections using the following probes:
- ALK (2p23) Dual Color Break Apart Rearrangement Probe (Abbott Molecular)
- ROS1 (6q22) Dual Color Break Apart Rearrangement Probe (Abbott Molecular)

Fifty (50) interphase nuclei were analyzed for each probe set. Results were correlated with H&E stained slides to ensure analysis of tumor cells.

CRITERIA FOR POSITIVE RESULTS
ALK FISH: ≥15% of cells with split signals (>2 signal diameters apart) or isolated 3' signals
ROS1 FISH: ≥15% of cells with split signals (>2 signal diameters apart) or isolated 3' signals

RESULTS

ALK (2p23) FISH Analysis:
- No ALK rearrangement detected
- 2-4 copies of intact ALK signals observed per cell
- 0% of cells showed split or isolated signals
- Classification: ALK NEGATIVE

ROS1 (6q22) FISH Analysis:
- No ROS1 rearrangement detected
- 2-4 copies of intact ROS1 signals observed per cell
- 0% of cells showed split or isolated signals
- Classification: ROS1 NEGATIVE

INTERPRETATION
This tumor is NEGATIVE for both ALK and ROS1 gene rearrangements by FISH analysis. The increased copy numbers (2-4 copies) of both ALK and ROS1 genes were noted in tumor cells, which may represent polysomy or focal amplification. The clinical significance of these copy number gains is unclear at this time.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
ALK and ROS1 rearrangements are important therapeutic targets in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Patients with tumors harboring these alterations may benefit from targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors. This tumor is negative for both rearrangements, indicating that ALK inhibitors (e.g., crizotinib, alectinib, brigatinib) and ROS1 inhibitors (e.g., crizotinib, entrectinib) are not indicated based on these results.

LIMITATIONS
FISH analysis detects only rearrangements involving the ALK and ROS1 genes. Other alterations such as point mutations or small insertions/deletions are not detected by this method. False negative results may occur if tumor cells comprise <20% of the sample or if variant rearrangements are present.
